title: Finite quotient preserves ordinary open support
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, an open immersion j:X→Y, a nonnegative index n, a left adjoint L to the specified finite module inverse image [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and its adjunction adj. For every completed-coefficient module M on X, adj.counit is invertible at the quotient of exponent n+1 of the actual completed-coefficient open extension of M [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. There is no flatness or completeness assumption on M.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, open-factor normalization: the ordinary section-normalized quotient/open map.

proof.text: Use the canonical constant-ring inverse-image isomorphism for the finite coefficient ring. Transposing twice identifies its direct image with the specified coefficient direct image, so uniqueness gives an isomorphism of their left adjoints.

Transpose the completed coefficient projection identity to get the coefficient square. The proved scalar-restriction/pullback isomorphism identifies the two composite right adjoints. Uniqueness of their left adjoints gives actual completed open extension followed by quotient ≅ quotient on the open followed by L.

Present finite extension as an equivalence followed by slice extension. The open is subterminal, hence the slice unit is invertible and extension is fully faithful. Transport this to L. Its counit is invertible on its essential image; the preceding comparison puts the quotient object there. This also covers empty and identity opens and zero modules.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryFiniteQuotientOpenSupport {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (n : ℕ)
    (L : normalizedDVRModules l E X n ⥤ normalizedDVRModules l E Y n)
    (adj : L ⊣ integralOperationsLevelPullback l E j n)
    (M : scalarReductionSource l E X) :
    IsIso (adj.counit.app ((unrestrictedIntegralReductionFunctor l E Y n).obj
      ((PurCompactSupport.openExtension (PurCompactSupport.completed l E) j).obj M)))
